question: In which year did Indian Railways start its first computerised reservation in New Delhi?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1986**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Indian Railways launched its first **computerised reservation system in New Delhi** in the year **1986**.
 
• This system was introduced to streamline ticket booking and reduce manual errors in the process.
 
• The initiative marked a major technological advancement in the Indian Railways sector, improving efficiency and customer experience.
 
• With this system, passengers could book tickets via computerised terminals, replacing the old manual ticketing system.
 
• This development paved the way for further advancements, including the introduction of online ticket booking systems in later years.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Computerised Reservation System (CRS):**

 
 
• CRS is a software-based system used for managing and booking tickets efficiently in transport industries.
 
• It ensures real-time updates on seat availability and reduces the chances of overbooking.
 
• The system integrates ticket booking, cancellation, and refund processes seamlessly.
 
 
 
• **IRCTC:**
 
 
• Indian Railways Catering and Tourism Corporation (IRCTC) was later established in 1999 to manage online ticketing services.
 
• IRCTC provides a platform for booking train tickets, catering services, and tourism packages.
 
 
 
• **Indian Railways and Technology:**
 
 
• Indian Railways has continuously integrated technology to modernize operations, including GPS tracking, e-ticketing, and automated train monitoring systems.
 
• These advancements aim to enhance passenger convenience and operational efficiency.
 
 
 
• **Global Context:**
 
 
• Computerised reservation systems were first introduced globally in the airline industry during the late 1950s.
 
• Indian Railways adopted similar concepts to improve transport service delivery within the country.
